expression: Piecewise((0, F_app <= mu_s*N), (F_app - mu_k*N, F_app > mu_s*N))
symbol_descriptions: Net horizontal force available to accelerate the block
Normal force pressing the block to the surface
derivation_notes: From Newton's second law with Coulomb friction: while the applied force does not exceed the static limit mu_s*N the block stays static (net force zero); once exceeded, kinetic friction mu_k*N opposes motion, giving net force F_app - mu_k*N.
scenario_text: A block rests on a horizontal surface and is pushed by a steadily increasing horizontal force. As long as the applied force stays below the static friction limit the block does not move, but once the threshold is exceeded it begins to accelerate under kinetic friction. The net driving force therefore behaves differently in the two regimes. We model the net accelerating force as a function of the applied push.

dependent_variable.description: Net horizontal force available to accelerate the block

independent_variables.description: Normal force pressing the block to the surface

expression: Piecewise((0, F_app <= mu_s*N), (F_app - (mu_k + (mu_s - mu_k)*exp(-((F_app - mu_s*N)/(mu_k*N))/v_ref))*N, F_app > mu_s*N))
symbol_descriptions: Net horizontal force available to accelerate the block
Normal force pressing the block to the surface
Stribeck transition scale controlling how quickly friction drops from static to kinetic as sliding develops
derivation_notes: Real dry friction does not jump discontinuously from mu_s*N to mu_k*N at breakaway; instead the effective friction coefficient decays smoothly from static toward kinetic (Stribeck effect) as the block starts sliding, parameterized by how far the drive exceeds the static limit.
change_summary: The abrupt static-to-kinetic friction discontinuity is replaced by a smooth exponential (Stribeck-type) crossover of the effective coefficient, giving a continuous net force just past breakaway while still reducing to F_app - mu_k*N far above threshold.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The friction coefficient switches instantaneously and discontinuously from mu_s to mu_k exactly at the breakaway point.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Asperity contacts detach and relubricate over a finite sliding onset, so the effective friction coefficient relaxes continuously from mu_s to mu_k (Stribeck curve) rather than jumping.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: As v_ref -> 0 the exponential collapses to a step, recovering F_app - mu_k*N immediately above threshold; far above threshold the exponential vanishes and the successor equals the parent exactly.

expression: Piecewise((0, F_app <= mu_s*N), (F_app - (mu_k + (mu_s - mu_k)*exp(-((F_app - mu_s*N)/(mu_k*N))/v_ref))*N*(1 + alpha_v*((F_app - mu_s*N)/(mu_k*N))), F_app > mu_s*N))
symbol_descriptions: Net horizontal force available to accelerate the block
Normal force pressing the block to the surface
Stribeck transition scale controlling how quickly friction drops from static to kinetic as sliding develops
Velocity-strengthening (viscous friction) coefficient governing the linear rise of friction with sliding speed once kinetic sliding is established
derivation_notes: Beyond the Stribeck drop, real sliding friction rises again at higher sliding speeds due to viscous/velocity-strengthening effects; using the excess-force proxy for sliding speed adds a linear term that lifts the kinetic friction above its floor.
change_summary: Multiplied the friction magnitude by a velocity-strengthening factor (1 + alpha_v*(excess force)/(mu_k*N)), preserving the piecewise Stribeck structure while adding the missing high-speed viscous friction rise.
